new_statements.citation: SIL PNG Branch. 2004 [data checked by Robert Conrad, March 1992]. Organised Phonology Data: May River Iwam (Iwam) Language [IWM], Ambunti - East Sepik Province. Ukarumpa: Summer Institute of Linguistics. 4 pp.
new_statements.locator: p. 3, section 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)'; p. 4 'Conventions: Orthographic'
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File (4 pp., the PDF's metadata gives the Author 'SIL PNG Branch', created 26 Aug 2004; text layer present, extracted with extracted text). Page 3 reads exactly: 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length) / Stress is phonemic at the word level. / 'humus 'house' hu'run 'ashes' / pe'u 'fish' 'peu 'skin''; page 4 under 'Conventions: Orthographic': 'Stress is not.' The reported quote is verbatim (the '[..]' bridges the syllable-pattern and phonological-conventions material between the two loci). Surrounding context read: header 'Organised Phonology Data / May River Iwam (Iwam) Language [IWM] / Ambunti - East Sepik Province / Sepik Ramu Phylum; Upper Sepik Stock; Iwam Family / Major villages: Araik…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress in May River Iwam is lexically contrastive (phonemic): its position is not predictable and distinguishes words (e.g. initial-stressed 'humus 'house' vs final-stressed hu'run 'ashes'; pe'u 'fish' vs 'peu 'skin'). Conrad 1972 (same analyst, read in snippet) adds that the contrast is realised only in isolation or phrase-final position; phrase-medially word stress shifts to the final syllable (to the penult before the possessive clitic -ni).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said in the OPD or in the recovered Conrad 1972 footnote.
new_statements.exceptions: Conrad 1972 fn.: 'word stress is contrastive only when words are in isolation or when they occur phonological phrase-final. Non phrase-final word stress shifts to the ultima unless the word occurs with the possessive clitic [-ni], in which case the stress shifts to the penult.' OPD p.4 notes /p/ may be a fricative 'rarely on unstressed syllables'.
new_statements.domain_note: Contrast holds for the word in citation form / phonological-phrase-final position; neutralised to word-final stress in non-phrase-final position (Conrad 1972). LAPSyD reports second-hand that Laycock (1965) heard stress on the first syllable, but Conrad & Dye 1975 state Laycock's 1965 'Iwam' data are Sepik Iwam [iws], whose own SIL descriptions (Laszlo & Rehburg 1970; Sepik Iwam OPD) indeed give non-contrastive, usually initial stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Target is May River Iwam [iwm] = iwam1256. The quoted OPD is explicitly 'May River Iwam (Iwam) Language [IWM]' (villages Araik, Mowi, Iyomempwi, Aumi; data checked by R. Conrad), and Conrad 1972 is explicitly 'Iwam (or May River)' (Glottolog 5.1 mis-tags Conrad 1972 as Sepik Iwam). Caution on Laycock 1965: Conrad & Dye 1975 fn.21 say Laycock's 'Iwam' phonology describes Sepik Iwam [iws] = sepi1255 (Laycock himself treated the two as dialects of one language); the Sepik Iwam SIL sources saved under sister_language_SepikIwam_iws/ give NON-contrastive, usually initial (alternating) stress - a genuinely different system from May River Iwam's phonemic stress, so second-hand 'initial stress' reports citing Laycock 1965 should not be attributed to iwam1256.

readall_conflicts: The only listed work (Laycock 1965) could not be opened, so no new first-hand statement was obtained. A latent tension exists in second-hand reports: LAPSyD 407 paraphrases Laycock 1965 as hearing stress on the first syllable, while the catalog's existing statement (SIL OPD 2004, checked by Conrad: 'Stress is phonemic at the word level', with minimal pairs 'humus/hu'run, pe'u/'peu) and the Conrad 1972 footnote recovered earlier ('word stress is contrastive only when words are in isolation or phonological phrase-final; non phrase-final word stress shifts to the ultima.. [with -ni] to the penult') describe contrastive, lexically placed stress. Two things soften this: (a) Conrad & Dye 1975 fn. 21 identify Laycock's Iwam as Sepik Iwam [iws], a different languoid whose own SIL OPD says 'Stress is usually on the first syllable' and whose Laszlo & Rehburg 1970 statement calls stress non-contrastive with first-and-alternating placement -- so the initial-stress paraphrase most likely belongs to sepi1255, not iwam1256; (b) LAPSyD's wording is hedged ('seems to be heard'). Laycock 1965 (per Laycock & Z'graggen 1975: 745) also states Iwam is not tonal, which agrees with the OPD's silence on tone. No contradiction is asserted for May River Iwam.
